Insights

What 6,900+ live listings leave out.

Every live SaaS listing in AWS Marketplace, read through the public Discovery API. At most two per seller. Counts of fields anyone can check, not opinions about any product.

77%

price only in “Units”

Procurement cannot tell what one unit buys.

80%

name no AWS service

Engineers cannot judge fit from the page.

74%

have no security or compliance term

The first thing a security reviewer looks for.

69%

have no deployment or setup language

No path from Subscribe to first result.

89%

have no customer review

No third-party proof on the page.

3%

declare MCP

Agent builders search for it by name.

SOURCE · AWS Marketplace Discovery API, snapshot 29 September 2026. Every SaaS listing in every category, at most two per seller (n = 6,966). Public listing data only; counts of observable fields, not opinions about any product.

How this was built

Method, and what it cannot tell you.

  • Source: AWS Marketplace Discovery API, read-only, public data. Snapshot 29 September 2026.
  • Population: every live SaaS listing in every category, capped at two per seller so large sellers do not skew it. n = 6,966.
  • Checks: fixed word and field checks, applied identically to every listing.
  • Publication rule: only aggregates. No single listing's score is published.

Limits

Keyword checks produce false negatives. A listing can describe its security in words the checker does not match. We have not measured how often. Read each percentage as “missing, as far as a word-and-field check can tell”.

The score is not a rating of the product. A good product can have a poor listing. It is not an AWS score and does not predict approval, search placement or sales.

The “typical” score reflects the checker. It gives zero for anything it cannot match, so it runs low by design. Use it to place a listing, not to grade one.
